data.title: Installation Support Coordinator
data.description:
Bij DeWarmte maken we slimme en betaalbare warmtepompen waarmee we woningen van het gas af helpen. We groeien hard en voeren steeds meer installaties uit. En hoe meer installaties we doen, hoe belangrijker het wordt dat onze installateurs snel geholpen worden als ze ergens tegenaan lopen.

Daarom zoeken we een Installation Support Coordinator.

Jij bent tijdens installaties het eerste aanspreekpunt voor onze installateurs. Je hoeft niet ieder technisch probleem zelf op te kunnen lossen. Jouw kracht zit vooral in snel begrijpen wat er speelt, bepalen wat er nodig is en zorgen dat de juiste persoon in actie komt.

Zie jezelf een beetje als de luchtverkeersleider van onze installaties: er gebeurt veel tegelijk, verschillende vragen hebben verschillende prioriteiten en jij houdt het overzicht.

Wat ga je doen?

Installateurs kunnen tijdens hun werk tegen allerlei vragen aanlopen. Soms kun je die zelf direct beantwoorden. Soms heb je werkvoorbereiding, engineering, service of een andere collega nodig. Jij zorgt dat de installateur zo snel mogelijk verder kan.

Concreet betekent dat dat je:

  • het eerste aanspreekpunt bent voor installateurs met vragen tijdens een installatie;

  • snel uitzoekt wat er precies aan de hand is en hoe urgent het is;

  • eenvoudige vragen zelf oplost;

  • bepaalt wie er nodig is als je de vraag niet zelf kunt beantwoorden;

  • zorgt voor een duidelijke overdracht naar de juiste collega;

  • urgente vragen actief blijft volgen totdat er een oplossing is;

  • installateurs op de hoogte houdt van de voortgang;

  • supportvragen en oplossingen goed registreert;

  • terugkerende problemen signaleert en bespreekt met de betrokken teams;

  • helpt om werkinstructies en veelvoorkomende oplossingen beter vast te leggen.

Je werkt daarbij veel samen met onder andere werkvoorbereiding, engineering, service en onze commerciële teams.

Wat maakt jou goed in deze rol?

Voor deze functie zoeken we niet per se iemand met jarenlange technische ervaring. Veel belangrijker is dat je snel kunt schakelen en goed overzicht houdt.

Je krijgt gedurende de dag verschillende vragen op je af. Jij kunt bepalen wat nú moet worden opgelost, wat kan wachten en wie je waarvoor nodig hebt. En als je iets bij een collega neerlegt, blijf je betrokken totdat duidelijk is hoe de installateur verder kan.

We denken dat je goed bij deze rol past als je:

  • energie krijgt van regelen, coördineren en problemen oplossen;

  • rustig blijft als er meerdere dingen tegelijk spelen;

  • snel hoofd- van bijzaken kunt onderscheiden;

  • makkelijk contact legt met verschillende soorten collega's;

  • duidelijk en praktisch communiceert;

  • verantwoordelijkheid neemt en dingen niet zomaar over de schutting gooit;

  • gestructureerd werkt en openstaande acties goed bijhoudt;

  • nieuwsgierig bent en graag wilt begrijpen hoe dingen werken;

  • goed Nederlands spreekt.

Ongeveer 1 tot 2 jaar werkervaring is mooi meegenomen, bijvoorbeeld in een operationele of coördinerende functie. Technische kennis van warmtepompen is geen vereiste. We kunnen je leren hoe onze producten en installaties werken. Belangrijker is dat jij snel leert en ervoor zorgt dat een vraag bij de juiste persoon terechtkomt.

Hoe ziet succes eruit?

Het belangrijkste is dat onze installateurs snel en goed geholpen worden en zo min mogelijk stil komen te staan doordat ze op een antwoord wachten.

Daarbij kijken we bijvoorbeeld naar hoe snel supportvragen worden opgepakt, of je de juiste prioriteiten stelt, of vragen bij de juiste collega's terechtkomen en hoe goed je openstaande vragen opvolgt.

Maar we willen ook steeds beter worden. Als jij merkt dat dezelfde vraag iedere week terugkomt, verwachten we niet dat je hem alleen iedere week opnieuw beantwoordt. Je zoekt samen met het team uit hoe we het probleem structureel kunnen oplossen.

Daar ligt voor jou veel ruimte om de rol verder uit te bouwen. Je helpt niet alleen individuele installateurs, maar kijkt ook naar de hele inbound support flow: hoe komen vragen binnen, hoe bepalen we de prioriteit, wie pakt wat op, hoe houden we overzicht en hoe zorgen we dat kennis niet verloren gaat?

Wat bieden we?

  • Een salaris tussen €3.000 en €4.000 bruto per maand op basis van 40 uur.

  • Een werkdag van 08:00 tot 16:30 uur.

  • Een werkplek op ons kantoor in Den Haag.

  • Veel verantwoordelijkheid en vrijheid om je werk goed in te richten.

  • De kans om veel te leren over warmtepompen en installatietechniek.

  • Lunch op kantoor.

  • Laptop en telefoon.

  • Regelmatige teamactiviteiten, van borrels tot onze jaarlijkse winter trip.

  • De mogelijkheid om mee te groeien met een bedrijf dat nog volop in ontwikkeling is.

Je komt terecht in een omgeving waar we snel schakelen, elkaar helpen en niet wachten tot iemand anders een probleem oplost. Zie je iets dat beter kan? Dan horen we dat graag. En nog liever zien we dat je helpt om het ook daadwerkelijk beter te maken.

Compensation: €3K – €4K per month

data.title: Customer Experience Manager
data.description:
Over DeWarmte

Wij zijn DeWarmte. Wij maken het makkelijk om afscheid te nemen van gas voor verwarming en warm water. Dat doen we met slimme, design warmte-oplossingen én met een customer journey die het voor onze klanten van begin tot eind makkelijk maakt.

We groeien snel. Steeds meer klantgroepen kiezen voor DeWarmte en dat betekent dat ook onze customer journey steeds groter en complexer wordt. Van het eerste contact met Sales tot planning, installatie, onboarding, service en onderhoud: op ieder moment willen we het voor onze klanten zo makkelijk mogelijk maken om van het gas af te gaan. Dat betekent goed advies, duidelijke communicatie, ondersteuning en aandacht bij elke stap.

Jouw bijdrage aan onze missie

Als Customer Experience Manager ben je verantwoordelijk voor de kwaliteit en consistentie van de totale customer experience. Van digitale tot persoonlijke interacties: jij bewaakt de kwaliteit van alle processen die onze customer journey direct raken. Daarom zoeken we iemand die over de hele organisatie heen kijkt, ontdekt waar het beter kan en ervoor zorgt dat verbeteringen ook daadwerkelijk worden gerealiseerd.

Jij bent binnen DeWarmte de functionele eigenaar van Customer Experience. Je bepaalt samen met de organisatie wat onze CX-standaard is, brengt systematisch in kaart waar we daar niet aan voldoen en zorgt dat de belangrijkste verbeteringen daadwerkelijk worden gerealiseerd. Je werkt hiervoor dwars door Marketing, Sales, Operations, Installation, Support & Service en Software heen.

Je hoeft daarbij niet ieder project zelf uit te voeren. Een verbetering kan bij jou liggen, bij een ‘Head of’ of bij iemand anders in de organisatie. Wat wél bij jou blijft liggen, is de accountability voor het realiseren van de verbetering: je zorgt voor een duidelijke eigenaar, doelstelling, deadlines en een kwaliteitsstandaard. Daarnaast bewaak je de voortgang en het resultaat. Je rapporteert rechtstreeks aan de CEO. Vanuit die positie werk je organisatiebreed en krijg je het mandaat om CX-verbeteringen over teams heen aan te jagen. Cross-functionele verbeterprojecten die over meerdere teams heen lopen, leid je in principe zelf.

Dat vraagt senioriteit. Je moet een Head kunnen challengen wanneer de customer experience niet goed genoeg is, maar net zo makkelijk zelf een review beantwoorden, een geautomatiseerde e-mail herschrijven of een (kleiner) verbeterproject van A tot Z uitvoeren.

 

Wat ga je doen?

  • Je beheert en verbetert onze bestaande customer journey en bijbehorende process maps en gebruikt deze om continu te identificeren waar de customer experience beter kan.

  • Je ontwikkelt samen met de verschillende teams onze CX-standaarden voor de belangrijkste customer touchpoints, bewaakt deze en spreekt teams erop aan wanneer de ervaring daar niet aan voldoet.

  • Je gebruikt reviews, klachten, customer feedback en operationele data om structurele problemen en verbeterkansen te identificeren en te prioriteren.

  • Je vertaalt deze inzichten naar een duidelijke, geprioriteerde CX-improvement roadmap.

  • Je initieert verbeterprojecten binnen Marketing, Sales, Operations, Installation, Support & Service, Software en andere teams en zorgt voor een duidelijke eigenaar, doelstelling, deadlines en kwaliteitsstandaard.

  • Je bewaakt de voortgang en het resultaat van deze verbeterprojecten en zorgt dat afgesproken verbeteringen daadwerkelijk worden gerealiseerd.

  • Cross-functionele CX-projecten die over meerdere teams heen lopen, leid je in principe zelf van analyse tot implementatie.

  • Je meet na implementatie of verbeteringen daadwerkelijk het gewenste effect op de customer experience hebben gehad.

  • Je bent verantwoordelijk voor onze aanpak rondom Google Reviews en Trustpilot: je zorgt dat reviews snel en goed worden beantwoord, dat problemen bij de juiste eigenaar terechtkomen en dat noodzakelijke opvolging snel plaatsvindt.

Hoe ziet succes eruit?

Makkelijk van het gas af. Dat moet de ervaring van onze klanten zijn gedurende de hele customer journey. Na de belangrijkste onderdelen van deze journey vragen we onze klanten actief om feedback. De scores op deze customer feedback vormen belangrijke KPI’s voor deze rol en laten zien waar de ervaring goed is en waar deze beter moet.

Onze Google- en Trustpilot-scores zijn belangrijke overkoepelende KPI’s voor de totale customer experience. Het doel is daarbij niet alleen om scores te verbeteren, maar vooral om de onderliggende customer experience structureel beter te maken.

Daarom kijken we ook naar hoe snel en goed customer feedback en reviews worden opgevolgd, hoeveel structurele customer pain points we oplossen en hoe snel en met welke kwaliteit de belangrijkste CX-improvement projecten worden gerealiseerd.

 

Wie zoeken we?

We zoeken iemand die continu ziet hoe het beter kan en vervolgens zorgt dat het ook beter wordt. Je combineert een hoge kwaliteitsstandaard en sterk analytisch vermogen met executiekracht. Je kunt diep de details induiken, maar ook bepalen waar de grootste impact ligt en op senior niveau door de hele organisatie verbeteringen realiseren.

Je hebt:

  • Meerdere jaren relevante ervaring binnen customer experience, customer operations, customer journey management, process improvement, projectmanagement of een vergelijkbare rol. Wat je aantoonbaar hebt gerealiseerd vinden we daarbij belangrijker dan je functietitel.

  • Ervaring met het verbeteren van customer journeys en processen, bij voorkeur in een snelgroeiende B2C-omgeving met een complexe operationele customer journey.

  • Aantoonbare ervaring met het omzetten van customer feedback en data naar concrete verbeteringen.

  • Een sterk analytisch vermogen: je kunt individuele klachten onderscheiden van structurele problemen, komt tot de root cause en weet waar je de meeste impact kunt maken.

  • Een uitzonderlijk oog voor detail en een hoge kwaliteitsstandaard. Je ziet inconsistenties, spelfouten, onduidelijke communicatie en afwijkingen van onze branding die anderen missen. Ook wanneer klanten tevreden zijn en duidelijke feedback opdroogt, blijf je zoeken naar hoe de customer experience nog beter kan.

  • Sterke projectmanagementvaardigheden. Je brengt structuur aan, maakt ownership en deadlines expliciet en krijgt meerdere verbeterinitiatieven daadwerkelijk over de finish.

  • De senioriteit en overtuigingskracht om stakeholders op verschillende niveaus te challengen en accountable te houden, ook wanneer zij niet aan jou rapporteren.

  • Een hands-on mentaliteit. Je vindt het prima om zelf een review te beantwoorden, een process map uit te pluizen of een (kleiner) project van A tot Z uit te voeren als dat nodig is.

  • Sterke communicatieve vaardigheden in het Nederlands en Engels. Duits is een plus.

Ervaring in een scale-up, consumer tech, energy, mobility, home services of een andere omgeving met een complexe operationele customer journey is een sterke plus.

Wat wij bieden

  • Een sleutelrol waarin je direct invloed hebt op hoe duizenden klanten DeWarmte ervaren.

  • Veel verantwoordelijkheid en ownership vanaf dag één, met een organisatiebreed mandaat en een directe rapportagelijn naar de CEO.

  • De vrijheid om verbeteringen door de hele organisatie heen te initiëren en te realiseren.

  • Een salaris van €4.500 tot €5.700 bruto per maand, afhankelijk van ervaring, plus deelname aan ons SAR-programma waarmee je meedeelt in de waardeontwikkeling van DeWarmte.

  • Een snelgroeiende scale-upomgeving waarin nog lang niet alles vastligt en je dus echt kunt bouwen.

  • De kans om nauw samen te werken met de CEO en Heads van de verschillende teams en je snel verder te ontwikkelen in het leiden van verbeteringen door de hele organisatie.

  • Een ambitieus team dat samenwerkt aan een duidelijke missie: zoveel mogelijk woningen van het gas afhalen.

  • Gezamenlijke lunches op kantoor.

  • Hybride werken: 3 dagen op kantoor, 2 dagen waar jij wilt.

  • Regelmatige teamuitjes en borrels, waaronder onze jaarlijkse stranddag en wintersport.

Interesse?

Wil jij ervoor zorgen dat de customer experience van DeWarmte net zo sterk groeit als het bedrijf zelf? Dan maken we graag kennis met je.

Compensation: €4.5K – €5.7K per month

data.title: People Operations Specialist
data.description:
Bouw mee aan de People-basis van DeWarmte

Bij DeWarmte maken we slimme en betaalbare warmtepompen waarmee we woningen van het gas af helpen. We groeien hard, in Nederland én daarbuiten. Ons team groeit mee en daarmee wordt een goede People-organisatie steeds belangrijker.

Daarom zoeken we een People Operations Specialist.

Iemand die ervoor zorgt dat alles rondom onze medewerkers goed geregeld is. Van contracten en payroll tot onboarding, HR-systemen en policies. Je houdt van structuur, werkt nauwkeurig en ziet snel waar dingen slimmer of beter kunnen.

We zijn een scale-up, dus je komt niet terecht in een omgeving waar alles al tot in detail is uitgedacht. Juist niet. Je helpt ons om de People-processen en systemen te bouwen die we nodig hebben om van ongeveer 60 naar 200 medewerkers te groeien.

Wat ga je doen?

Je wordt verantwoordelijk voor een groot deel van onze dagelijkse People Operations. Je zorgt dat zaken goed geregeld zijn voor medewerkers en managers, maar kijkt tegelijkertijd hoe we processen slimmer, eenvoudiger en schaalbaarder kunnen maken.

Je zorgt dat onze People-administratie klopt

Je maakt arbeidsovereenkomsten en andere HR-documenten, houdt personeelsgegevens up-to-date en zorgt dat wijzigingen correct worden verwerkt. Je werkt nauwkeurig en zorgt dat informatie makkelijk terug te vinden is.

Je coördineert payroll en arbeidsvoorwaarden

Je verzamelt en controleert de maandelijkse payrollmutaties en werkt samen met onze salarisadministrateur. Ook help je bij vragen over salaris, vakantiegeld, pensioen, verlof en andere arbeidsvoorwaarden.

Je maakt onboarding en offboarding soepel

Je zorgt dat nieuwe collega's goed kunnen starten en dat alles achter de schermen geregeld is. Ook bij uitdiensttreding zorg je dat het proces netjes wordt afgerond.

Je bouwt onze People-processen en systemen verder uit

We groeien snel en nog niet alles is geautomatiseerd of gestandaardiseerd. Je helpt bij het implementeren en verbeteren van ons HR-systeem en zorgt dat processen rondom bijvoorbeeld contracten, verlof, onboarding en employee data steeds slimmer worden ingericht.

Je helpt ons compliant te blijven

Je ondersteunt bij arbeidsrechtelijke en administratieve verplichtingen en zorgt dat documentatie en processen op orde zijn. Omdat DeWarmte uit meerdere entiteiten bestaat en internationaal groeit, krijg je ook te maken met verschillende arbeidsvoorwaarden en regelgeving.

Je ondersteunt medewerkers en managers

Je bent een praktisch aanspreekpunt voor dagelijkse People-vragen. Je helpt medewerkers verder en ondersteunt managers bij operationele HR-zaken.

Je zorgt voor inzicht

Je houdt People-data goed bij en helpt met rapportages over bijvoorbeeld headcount, verloop, verzuim en andere belangrijke People-data.

Wie zoeken we?

We zoeken iemand die energie krijgt van dingen goed regelen én verbeteren. Je hoeft niet overal al specialist in te zijn, maar je moet wel zelfstandig kunnen werken en comfortabel zijn in een omgeving waar nog niet voor alles een proces bestaat.

Je:

  • hebt een relevante HBO of WO opleiding afgerond

  • hebt een paar jaar relevante ervaring binnen HR / People Operations

  • hebt ervaring met HR-administratie, contracten en payrollprocessen

  • werkt gestructureerd en nauwkeurig

  • vindt het leuk om processen te verbeteren en structuur aan te brengen

  • kunt goed schakelen tussen verschillende onderwerpen en prioriteiten

data.title: Talent & People Partner
data.description:
Jij vindt de mensen die de warmte brengen

We nemen op dit moment zo'n vier mensen per maand aan, zonder recruiter. Onze People Director doet het erbij en er draait tijdelijk een externe sourcer mee. Dat gaat goed, maar het houdt geen stand bij het tempo dat we willen.

Daarom zoeken we jou. Recruitment is dit kwartaal ons bedrijfsdoel, niet één van de doelen maar hét doel.

Warmte zonder gas

Wist je dat wij onze warmtepompen zelf ontwerpen? Met een club van ruim zestig mensen bedenken we ze, assembleren we ze in Utrecht en installeren we ze zelf. Voor huiseigenaren door heel Nederland en sinds dit jaar ook in Duitsland. Vorig jaar won onze Pomp MP als enige warmtepomp ooit zowel de iF Design Award Gold als de Red Dot.

Elke week gaan er tientallen huizen van het gas af. Het doel is 10% van alle Nederlandse woningen, ongeveer 800.000 huizen. De vraag is er en het product staat. De rem zit op hoe snel we kunnen leveren.

Dat lukt niet zonder jou als Talent & People Partner.

 

Wat jij doet

80% van je werk is mensen aannemen. Niet als opstartfase, maar omdat werving nu de bottleneck van het bedrijf is en dat voorlopig blijft.

De andere 20% is hoe we het doen. Onboarding, hoe we gesprekken voeren, employer branding, welke tools we gebruiken. Daar ben je eigenaar van vanaf dag één, niet pas als recruitment een keer af is.

  • Je bent verantwoordelijk voor het hele proces, van eerste benadering tot getekend contract

  • Je zoekt zelf actief, via LinkedIn, referrals en wat er verder werkt per doelgroep

  • Je begeleidt hiring managers die goed zijn in hun vak, maar geen recruiters zijn

  • Je bent het aanspreekpunt voor de externe partijen waar we mee werken

  • Je richt Ashby zo in dat het proces sneller gaat in plaats van langzamer

Hoe je week eruitziet

De doelgroepen liggen ver uit elkaar en dat maakt dit werk interessant. De monteurs zitten niet op LinkedIn en vind je via Indeed, vakcommunities en soms Facebook. De sales-adviseurs zitten er wel. Voor Duitsland begint alles opnieuw.

 

Je werkt direct met de People Director, met de hoofden van installatie, service en sales, en met de oprichters. Korte lijnen is hier geen bullet uit een vacaturetekst. Het betekent dat je naar iemand toe loopt.

 

Wat je oplevert

Je kiest de kanalen per doelgroep, je bouwt Ashby om tot iets dat werkt, en je bepaalt hoe we gesprekken voeren en hoe iemand hier zijn eerste weken doorkomt.

Over twee jaar heb je een recruitmentfunctie staan die je zelf hebt neergezet, in een bedrijf dat in die tijd is verdubbeld. Daar kun je de rest van je loopbaan naar wijzen.

 

Wat je meebrengt

  • Twee tot vijf jaar recruitment-ervaring. Bureau of in-house, allebei prima

  • Je hebt zelf met een ATS gewerkt en weet hoe je er een proces in bouwt

  • Je vindt het leuk om structuur te brengen in een omgeving die snel verandert

  • Je vindt het oké dat wat maandag prioriteit is, vrijdag anders kan liggen

  • Nederlands en Engels. Duits is een pré, want Duitsland komt eraan

Ervaring met technische profielen of de installatiebranche is een grote pré. Heb je die niet, maar beheers je het vak? Bel dan even. Twijfel je of je past? Bel of app Anniek op 06 4850 0142.

 

Wat je krijgt

  • Een marktconform salaris, afhankelijk van je ervaring

  • 27 vakantiedagen bij fulltime, plus 8% vakantiegeld dat we maandelijks uitbetalen

  • Laptop en telefoon

  • Maandag, woensdag en vrijdag op kantoor in Den Haag, dinsdag en donderdag thuis

  • Gezamenlijke lunch op kantoor en de jaarlijkse winterreis met het hele bedrijf

Wat je opbouwt

Je deelt mee in de waardegroei van DeWarmte via ons SAR-programma. Kort gezegd: je krijgt geen aandelen, maar wel het financiële voordeel daarvan. Wordt het bedrijf ooit verkocht, dan krijg jij uitbetaald hoeveel het meer waard is geworden sinds de dag dat jij begon. Hoe eerder je instapt, hoe groter dat verschil kan zijn.

 

Met wie je werkt

Je rapporteert aan Anniek Sluis, People Director en de eerste HR-aanstelling van dit bedrijf. Zij bouwt de People-functie op en jij wordt haar eerste collega. Daarnaast werk je met Daan Köster (installatie), Lars Steverink (service), Eyso de Vries (sales) en met de oprichters Sander Wapperom en Auke de Vries.

Hoe het gaat

We nemen op dit moment ongeveer vier mensen per maand aan, en de teams die we nu bouwen moeten staan voor de piek aan het eind van het jaar. Reageer je deze week, dan zit je er nog bij.

  • 1. Bel of app Anniek op 06 4850 0142, of stuur je cv. Een motivatiebrief hoeft niet.

  • 2. Een online kennismaking van een half uur.

  • 3. Een gesprek bij ons op kantoor in Den Haag, met een case en een persoonlijkheidstest.

  • 4. Een culture check met een paar toekomstige collega's, online of meteen aansluitend.

We laten je zo snel mogelijk weten waar je staat. Duurt het een keer langer, dan hoor je van ons waarom. Anniek is ook je toekomstige collega, dus je spreekt vanaf het begin de juiste persoon

items.question: What are the main challenges a Principal Technical Program Manager faces when aligning cross-functional teams on complex projects?
items.answer: A Principal Technical Program Manager often encounters the challenge of ensuring that diverse teams—such as engineering, product, design, and operations—are aligned on priorities, timelines, and deliverables for large-scale initiatives. This requires strong communication and negotiation skills, as well as the ability to manage conflicting interests and dependencies. Additionally, adapting to shifting business goals while maintaining clear project direction is a key part of the role. Successfully navigating these challenges enables the program manager to drive impactful outcomes and foster collaboration across the organization.

qa.question:
I work at a mid-size (~1500 employees) health tech company mostly focused on SaaS web applications.

I'm currently a developer/team lead/scrum master who has been getting further and further from the keyboard. I have about 8 years of experience but it's been a while since I've made meaningful contributions to the code base. I've realized I may not be the strongest coder and am better at the higher level engineering problems like architecting, figuring out how to accomplish work, talking to the right people, making the right connections, and basically greasing the wheel for my team members.

Recently the company has been making a big push to adopt agile practices (please save the agile hate for another thread). It's something my team and I have already been doing for a while so we're ahead of the curve here.

Anyways, they've introduced this new role of "Engineering Operations" and put someone in that position who seems to be setting the new standards for how our engineering organization operates. A lot of it right now has to do with these new agile processes, but I imagine as the rest of the org settles in and gets more accustom to these practices there will be less of a focus on agile and more on engineering practices/standards.

I think a lot of my strengths lie more in the people/process world than the coding world. I'm still very interested in tech and want to stay technical, but I'm maybe not the rockstar developer cranking out code all the time.

I like to think about how we complete work more efficiently, how we architect and test our services, how engineering teams work together to accomplish shared goals, how developers work with product managers and UX to be more cross-functional and vertically integrated. Stuff like that.

Is there a path for me to grow these skills and focus more on that than actual coding? Am I still going to have to solve ridiculous coding puzzles in future interviews if I go down this path? The biggest thing I'm scared of is letting my coding skills atrophy and not being hirable in the future.

Thanks for any advice

answer.text: You are too young in your career to distance yourself from technical contributions. I reccomend course correcting for continued job options and hireability

extra_snippets: You've described my career path about eight years ago. I work for a Fortune 100 company everybody's heard of, so the role does exist, it's just in a weird space and nobody ever writes a job description for it. If it were a Venn diagram, my role would be somewhere at the intersection of technical program manager, software engineer, and a product manager. My work started with something called "engineering operations" which was basically "devops".

items.question: What Does a Director of Engineering Do?
items.answer: A director of engineering is the head of the engineering team or department. This is a leadership position in upper management, but unlike other director roles, the director or engineering plays an active part in the development of a project. They work with their team of engineers to set goals, plan projects, build a timeline, and stay within budget. Their duties and responsibilities also include project management, hiring new team members, presenting budgets and plans to other departments, and meeting with upper-level management.

jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager - Technical Strategy Development
jobs.location: Mountain View, California, United States | San Diego, California, United States
jobs.description:
The Tech Strategic Programs organization delivers for Intuit and Tech Strategy by transforming and driving how our 10,000-person Technology ecosystem operates to accelerate outcomes for our customers.  This high performing team works with senior leaders and partners across the company.  We focus on strategic planning, the operating rhythm, executive narratives, workforce programs, and developing portfolio insights to accelerate the delivery of the highest priority areas for growth and customer impact leveraging emerging technology.

 

We are looking for creative problem solvers with a bias for action, an ability to analyze and connect the dots between multitudinous  sources of data and information, and a strong desire to drive tangible business impact. As a Principal Technical Program Manager, you will work alongside executive leaders to construct and deliver board and C-level content. You will also have an opportunity to work across the broader Product, Marketing, Finance, and Business segment communities to help innovate and drive change in how we operate. This position requires strong strategic problem solving and communication skills, the ability to inﬂuence and develop productive partnerships at all levels of the organization, solid business and technical acumen and a strong understanding of Intuit’s mission and values.


Responsibilities


  • Orchestrate development of executive-level presentations and content to be used by the CTO  in board meetings, CEO Staff meetings, and other forums

  • Partner with senior leaders and cross-functional teams (e.g. Product, Marketing, Finance, Business segments) to outline data-driven strategic frameworks decisions, and actionable recommendations

  • Lead strategy projects / work streams and new initiatives end-to-end, with limited guidance, from initial hypotheses to recommendation to operationalization

  • Develop narratives that highlight the outcomes delivered across the Tech Ecosystem and their connection to strategy

  • Build and maintain strong relationships across the Tech Ecosystem and CTO staff to ensure that we are thinking holistically across multiple tech priorities and in line with our technology strategy.

  • Design and implement frameworks and operating models that accelerate decision making, sharing of best practices, and operational excellence at scale across tech.  


Qualifications


  • 7-10 years of relevant experience in delivering signiﬁcant strategic and operational impact across an organization

  • Strategy and operations experience at a high growth startup, management consulting experience or strategic/analytical roles at large companies is desired

  • Proven track record in leveraging data, developing insight-backed hypotheses and driving learning plans to build compelling business cases

  • Demonstrated business and technical acumen, preferably in a SaaS or platform technology company.

  • Ownership mindset with an ability to convert strategic plans into actions, drive projects to completion, and sweat the details to deliver the outcome

  • Experienced change management leader who is able to inﬂuence and build trust across a highly cross-functional organization (peers, executives and working teams) to accelerate outcomes

  • Excellent communicator with strong presentation skills and compelling storytelling abilities; feel very comfortable leading and facilitating workshops and monthly/quarterly business reviews with executives and teams

  • Highly self-motivated, thrives in ambiguity and able to manage multiple projects with little day to day direction

  • Well-rounded interpersonal skills with the capacity to build relationships with senior stakeholders and collaborate across with team members across varying levels

  • Ability to generate innovative insights, ideas, and opportunities that drive tangible business outcomes

  • FinTech and/or SaaS experience a plus, but not required


Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position will be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

The expected base pay range for this position is:
Mountain View $238,000 - $322,000
San Diego, CA $219,500- $297,000

jobs.title: Director, Engineering Operations
jobs.description:
Job Responsibilities:

The Director of Engineering Operations is responsible for overseeing the Operations engineering team’s work efforts including technical review and field commissioning of new construction, renovation projects, and significant system upgrades, as well as advanced technical troubleshooting of the Johns Hopkins Health System’s and School of Medicine’s healthcare, teaching and research facilities. This includes developing, implementing, and managing comprehensive plans from design review through construction, functional testing, operational handover, and post-project troubleshooting. The Director ensures that all building systems, including but not limited to HVAC, electrical, plumbing, medical gas, fire suppression, and building automation systems, meet performance specifications, regulatory requirements (such as The Joint Commission, NFPA, AAALAC, etc.) and the operational needs of a mission critical and complex academic medical center environment.

The Director coordinates troubleshooting efforts for equipment and complex systems, working in close collaboration with the engineering teams' shops. The Director actively participates in developing sustainability initiatives focused on achieving institutional goals and works with the engineering teams for implementation. Formally participates in campus utility master planning efforts. This role requires extensive technical expertise, strong organizational skills, a collaborative spirit, and a comprehensive understanding of healthcare and research operations and compliance. Prepares staffing and budgetary plans and manages resources to achieve department goals. Performs general managerial duties such as supervising staff, planning, scheduling, budgeting, data analysis, reporting, and performing presentations. Coordinates training and other programs to develop and enhance individual technical and management skills and to ensure the retention and career advancement of employees in the department. The Director, Engineering Operations works in close collaboration with the Director, Engineering Design to ensure operational team experience informs the various JHHS standard specifications and future engineering design efforts. The Director, Engineering Operations, performs these responsibilities with minimal supervision of the Executive Director, JHHS Facilities Management.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering or related field. Master’s degree preferred.
  • 10 or more years including 7 or more years related work experience in a supervisory or managerial capacity.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) preferred

Salary Range: $145,000 to $200,000 per year. Compensation will be commensurate with equity and experience for roles of similar scope and responsibility.

We are committed to creating a welcoming and inclusive environment, where we embrace and celebrate our differences, where all employees feel valued, contribute to our mission of serving the community, and engage in equitable healthcare delivery and workforce practices.

Johns Hopkins Health System and its affiliates are drug-free workplace employers.

GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As Director, Engineering, Platform Operations & Productivity, you'll own three functions that all require hands-on technical depth, not just people management.

Platform Staff is a small, senior, AI-native team that moves to wherever the organization needs the most leverage, from standing up early scaffolding for an initiative, to taking on a high-impact customer request that doesn't fit any existing team's charter, to stepping directly into a production crisis until it's resolved.

This role is for a technical engineering director who has personally built distributed systems, not only managed people who did. You'll use clear metrics, strong operating rhythms, and direct technical judgment so these teams deliver predictable outcomes without relying on one-person heroics.

What you’ll do

  • Own outcomes for Git & Gitaly Operations, including hiring and developing the Manager, Git & Gitaly Operations, and holding the function to its reliability bar across Self-Managed, GitLab Dedicated, and SaaS.
  • Own outcomes for Nonlinear Productivity, also known as Friction Elimination, including hiring and developing the Manager, Nonlinear Productivity, and holding the function to measurable metric movement rather than activity.
  • Build and oversee Platform Staff directly as a small, senior team that uses AI-assisted tools as a standard part of its work.
  • Assess, case by case, what Platform Staff picks up, such as a new team that needs bootstrapping, a customer request too specific for any existing team's charter, or a crisis that needs someone in the room immediately.
  • Assess when Platform Staff should hand work off to a permanent team once it's stable.
  • Set the technical bar across all three functions by personally reviewing distributed systems designs, friction-elimination fixes, and crisis management plans with equal depth.
  • Build the operating rhythm and metrics that keep all three functions running predictably, so none of them relies on any one person working unsustainable hours.
  • Represent all three functions to peer engineering stakeholders, and step in front of customers directly when Platform Staff is engaged mid-crisis.

What you’ll bring

  • Working knowledge of GitLab's development workflows and platform capabilities so you can assess productivity friction, operational trade-offs, and team needs in context.
  • Hands-on experience designing and shipping distributed systems personally, not only through teams you've managed.
  • A track record running highly effective engineering operations, including production reliability and incident management, at meaningful scale.
  • A track record driving measurable engineering productivity improvements across more than one team or organization.
  • Experience with AI-assisted development tools, and sound judgment about when they help a small team do work that would otherwise require a larger team.
  • People management experience across multiple managers or functions at once.
  • Ability to context-switch effectively across genuinely different problem types, including infrastructure operations, developer productivity, and ad hoc crisis response, sometimes in the same week.
  • A track record making staffing decisions that keep a high-leverage team intentionally small, and building alignment around those decisions rather than growing the team by default.

About the team

We work across three connected platform and productivity functions. Through Git & Gitaly Operations, we are responsible for the production reliability of the infrastructure layer underneath GitLab's own version control system. Through Nonlinear Productivity, we drive measurable improvements to GitLab's software development lifecycle and code-generation workflows. Through Platform Staff, we provide focused senior engineering capacity for high-leverage work that needs direct ownership before it can be stabilized or handed off to a permanent team.

Collectively, we help GitLab improve the reliability, productivity, and responsiveness of the platform that powers how our customers and GitLab team members build software.



How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

  • Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
  • Flexible Paid Time Off 
  • Team Member Resource Groups
  • Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Growth and Development Fund
  • Parental Leave

Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.

Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  

Privacy Policy: Please review our Recruitment Privacy Policy. Your privacy is important to us.

GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also GitLab’s EEO Policy and EEO is the Law. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know during the recruiting process.

Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!

We're looking for an experienced Technical Program Manager to build and run the program operating system for Figma's growing Internal AI Tooling portfolio. Reporting into the CIO PMO and embedded within the team driving this work, you'll partner closely with Product and Engineering leaders to translate an emerging roadmap into coordinated, secure, and scalable capabilities used across Figma — bringing together Engineering, Security, Legal, Procurement, Data Engineering, Business Systems, IT, Enablement, and business teams.

You'll create clarity across this system by establishing lightweight planning and governance, aligning teams around shared milestones and decisions, and ensuring initiatives move from intake through release and operational handoff with clear ownership and measurable outcomes — shaping not only what gets delivered, but also how Figma evaluates, builds, releases, and operates internal AI capabilities as the portfolio grows.

The ideal candidate can bring structure to an ambiguous, fast-moving environment without introducing unnecessary process, and can lead complex work through influence rather than direct authority.

This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States. 

What you'll do at Figma:

  • Translate the Product Manager's roadmap and prioritized outcomes into integrated program plans, milestones, release schedules, decision points, and clear ownership
  • Manage execution of the Internal AI Tooling roadmap across technical teams and business stakeholders
  • Operationalize a transparent intake and routing process so requests have a defined problem, expected business outcome, delivery path, risk profile, and accountable owner before work begins
  • Establish and facilitate lightweight planning and execution cadences, including program reviews, dependency reviews, decision forums, release-readiness reviews, and stakeholder updates
  • Maintain an integrated view of dependencies, risks, issues, assumptions, and decisions, driving timely resolution or escalation when work is blocked
  • Coordinate security reviews, legal and procurement milestones, data dependencies, vendor commitments, and business-system integrations so these workstreams are engaged at the appropriate stage of delivery
  • Ensure releases have appropriate acceptance criteria, operational ownership, support processes, runbooks, escalation paths, and feedback loops before handoff
  • Partner with Product and stakeholders to define measurable outcomes and provide clear reporting on delivery health, adoption readiness, operational performance, and realized impact

We'd love to hear from you if you have:

  • 5+ years of technical program management, or technical delivery experience in a cloud, SaaS, enterprise-technology, or internal-tools environment
  • Demonstrated experience leading complex programs across Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, Data, Business Systems, Operations, and business stakeholders
  • A track record of translating product roadmaps into integrated plans, milestones, dependencies, decision points, release schedules, and measurable outcomes while maintaining clear ownership boundaries between Product, Program, and Engineering
  • Technical fluency with enterprise systems, APIs, integrations, data flows, platform dependencies, identity and access, and software-delivery lifecycles. You do not need to be an engineer, but you should be able to engage credibly in technical planning and tradeoff conversations
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, facilitation, and influencing skills, with the ability to establish lightweight governance, present concise decisions and risks, and create accountability without relying on direct authority

While it's not required, it's an added plus if you also have:

  • Direct experience delivering internal AI tooling, platform, or product programs in a rapidly evolving technology environment
  • Experience with responsible AI, model governance, security, privacy, compliance, or AI risk-management frameworks
  • Familiarity with enterprise SaaS, middleware, low-code or no-code automation, identity platforms, data platforms, vendor evaluation, or procurement processes

About the role

We are hiring an Energy Scheduling & Portfolio Lead to own energy availability across Anthropic's non-cloud data center portfolio: contracted and available energy against planned compute, and the risk to it. This one central scheduling and portfolio role holds the live view of energy availability risk and energy availability need for workload management. You will be our counterpart to the LSEs, QSEs, scheduling coordinators, and suppliers in electricity and gas markets across jurisdictions; forecasting is an instrument of that view. You schedule and manage physical energy delivery — not financial instruments — including how much gas the portfolio needs to schedule, and keep energy supply and the workload plan in step with workload and site planning, energy origination, and data center operations. ESA counterparties operate the behind-the-meter plants; you manage their performance and our exposure. This role will also build processes and structures to ultimately support asset management across our energy portfolio. You are this function's first dedicated owner and will build its models and processes from zero.

Responsibilities:

  • Own the live view of energy availability risk and need: contracted, available, and committed energy and capacity at each site against planned load and ramp, by month and by hour where it matters; keep it current as deals sign, sites come online, and plans change, and close gaps and use surpluses with workload and site planning and energy origination.

  • Be the operational counterpart to our LSEs, QSEs, scheduling coordinators, and retail and wholesale suppliers in domestic ISO/RTOs, including ERCOT, and international power markets, and manage our participation in utility and ISO market programs.

  • Predict and track curtailment (utility, ISO, fuel, equipment, and contract-driven) for each site, and navigate shortage pricing and reliability events: ISO scarcity pricing, emergency procedures, conservation calls, and the notification and performance obligations under each ESA, PPA, utility agreement, and market program; coordinate the load response with site operations and workload planning, and track performance, compensation, and cost.

  • Oversee the portfolio's contracted or tariff-based load-flexibility capability and the contribution of this capability to Anthropic's ratepayer-protection commitment: curtailment and demand-response participation, flexible-interconnection and non-firm service commitments to utilities and ISOs, and the site-level playbooks for each; work with workload planning on what the compute can actually flex, and commit only where the workload plan supports it.

  • For the first operating sites, manage counterparty performance and Anthropic's exposure under the ESAs: outage notices, availability guarantees, liquidated damages, dispatch coordination, and the reporting behind them. Know the ESAs and utility load agreements we sign well enough to operate their scheduling, curtailment, availability, flexibility, and ratepayer-protection terms, and partner with legal and energy origination so new agreements are operable.

  • Determine how much gas the portfolio needs to schedule and build the portfolio's gas scheduling strategy for gas-fired behind-the-meter supply, nominations, hub and index pricing, pipeline capacity and constraints, and work through gas-plant outages and their effect on site availability, including by building relationships with external commodity partners.

  • Build Anthropic's energy forecasting as an instrument of the availability-risk view: consumption per site from the workload plan, site design, and ramp, and cost against ESA and PPA terms, market and natural gas prices, as the monthly and annual outputs the team and Finance need, including exposure to index-priced volume and the inputs energy origination needs to size new supply. Supply the energy-side inputs and checks that let Finance, Accounting, and Procurement Ops reconcile invoices and settlements against ESA, PPA, and tariff terms and explain the variance; this role will collaborate heavily with energy finance but will not have primary responsibility for financial management of the energy portfolio — the physical position is yours. Track the market information that moves our position — ISO/RTO prices, scarcity and reliability conditions, gas hub prices, ancillary and capacity costs, and tariff, interconnection, and market rule changes — and reflect it in the view.

  • Work cross-functionally: with energy finance on the financial management of the portfolio, with data center operations on site load, flexibility, and outages, and with other internal teams — workload and site planning, engineering and design, legal, procurement — so the energy position and the physical reality of each site stay aligned. Build and own the processes, data, and tooling for all of the above; partner with engineering and site operations on metering, telemetry, and load data so the availability view, forecasts, and settlements rest on measured consumption.

You may be a good fit if you:

  • Have 8+ years in energy markets, power scheduling, energy procurement, or utility / retail energy operations, including hands-on work with scheduling and settlement review in ERCOT, PJM, NYISO, MISO, or another ISO/RTO market.

  • Have worked at or directly with an LSE, QSE, scheduling coordinator, retail energy provider, or load-management desk, and know day-ahead and real-time scheduling, settlements, and curtailment / demand-response programs from the inside.

  • Read ESAs, PPAs, and utility large-load interconnection and service agreements fluently enough to operate their scheduling, availability, curtailment, and pricing terms and to model the exposure they create.

  • Can predict curtailment for a large load and navigate shortage pricing and reliability events — ISO scarcity pricing, emergency procedures, conservation calls — from experience, not from the rulebook.

  • Understand gas scheduling — nominations, hub pricing, pipeline constraints — and have worked through gas-fired plant outages and their effect on served load.

  • Have designed or operated load flexibility for a large load — curtailment, demand response, non-firm or flexible interconnection — and understand the large-load tariff provisions that protect other ratepayers (minimum demand charges, cost allocation, exit and stranded-cost provisions, study and collateral requirements) and how a load operates within them.

  • Have built or run energy consumption and cost forecasts for large loads — data centers, industrials, or a retail / wholesale portfolio — and can tie a forecast to contract terms and market prices.

  • Coordinate well across teams that do not report to you — workload planning, site operations, finance, legal, origination — and can give a clear picture of where energy availability stands against need and where it is at risk.

  • Have stood up a scheduling, portfolio, or operations function from scratch and built the models and processes it runs on.

  • Possess a bachelor's degree in a relevant domain (e.g., engineering, economics, energy, finance, data science) or equivalent practical experience.

It's a bonus if you have:

  • Experience with data center or other large, fast-ramping load in ERCOT, PJM, NYISO, MISO, or another ISO/RTO market.

  • Experience with behind-the-meter, islanded, or bridge-power configurations and how they schedule and settle differently from grid-served load, including managing counterparty performance under an ESA or tolling agreement — availability guarantees, outage reporting, liquidated damages, dispatch coordination.

  • Familiarity with hedging and risk management of energy cost — fixed-price, index, shaped, and block products — and with how hedges sit against physical consumption, enough to work fluently with Finance on it.

  • Familiarity with natural gas markets and hub pricing, with an emphasis on physical scheduling at regional basis hubs, gas-price indices, pipeline nominations and capacity.

  • Experience with energy data and metering systems, interval data, and building forecasting models from them.

  • Exposure to the regulatory and public-affairs side of large-load service — large-load tariff proceedings, interconnection rulemakings, or utility rate cases — and to utility and ISO demand-response, curtailment, and flexible-interconnection programs.

  • Prior experience standing up an operations or analytics function in a growing team.

About the Role:

We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to lead the systems, data, and process work behind how we bill, recognize revenue, close the books, and prove our controls work.

You won't be writing the code or drawing the architecture; you'll be deciding what gets built, in what order, and why it matters. This is a role for someone who wants to understand a business well enough to change how it runs: learning the objectives, processes, and system flows end to end, then shaping them into strategic technical programs with real owners, deliberate sequencing, and decisions that hold up under audit. You'll sit between Finance and Accounting on one side and Engineering, Data, and Product on the other, and you'll be accountable for making new revenue streams operable and auditable, from a pricing model on a slide to a billed invoice, a booked journal entry, and a control that passes testing.

You'll report to the Lead Technical Program Manager for Data, Biztech & AI Transformation, within EPD. You'll get high-level direction and clear priorities from your manager, and independent ownership of how the work actually gets delivered. You'll bring engineering-side rigor and platform thinking to finance problems, and work as part of a team modernizing how the whole company operates.

Most of your time will go to three things: making new product and pricing launches work end to end in the finance stack, running the platforms and data flows behind quote-to-cash and record-to-report, and driving the IT general controls (ITGC) program so controls are designed into systems up front rather than retrofitted after go-live.

This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. 

What You'll Achieve:

Act as Finance's technical counterpart on new product, pricing, and packaging launches, translating commercial models into requirements across order capture, rating and billing, tax, revenue recognition, and downstream reporting, and defining what "revenue-ready" means before go/no-go: who owns each piece, what's actually done versus asserted, and which risks are still cheap to fix

Broker the trade-off when a launch date and systems reality don't line up: a scoped manual workaround with an owner, a cost, and an expiration date, plus the path to the automated version. Then close the loop after launch on billing accuracy, exception rates, where revenue landed, whether the new controls actually operate, and what must be true to do this again at 10x volume

Independently own delivery and multi-quarter roadmaps for your finance systems programs, including ERP, billing and subscription management, CPQ, revenue subledger, procurement, and the reporting layer on top. Run the working groups that deliver them across Finance, Accounting, Engineering, Data, and Security, with clear accountability and updates leadership can read in two minutes

Run the operating rhythm: intake and prioritization, decision logs, early risk escalation, and a small set of metrics that show whether the work is actually improving anything, and flag early when committed scope and capacity don't line up

Map current-state processes and data lineage end to end and go after the breaks: reconciliation gaps, recurring manual journal entries, spreadsheets doing load-bearing work, competing sources of truth for the same metric. Partner with Data Engineering on the definitions and data contracts that let finance metrics tie cleanly to source systems, and hold the line when teams drift

Drive ITGC workstreams across in-scope financial systems: logical access and segregation of duties, change management, SDLC and CI/CD pipelines, job scheduling, and data interfaces. Partner with Internal Audit on scoping and control design, with a named owner for every control

Facilitate designing controls into new systems, systems changes, and launches before go-live with Controllership, Internal Audit, and Engineering, and serve as the systems-side point of contact for internal and external audit on ITGC walkthroughs and testing, translating between control language and engineering language, and driving deficiencies through root cause, named owners, evidence, and validation that the fix holds

Build AI-assisted workflows that expand what the teams around you can cover, and hold them to real standards: a defined task, a way to evaluate output quality, explicit human review gates on anything touching financial reporting, and documentation so someone else can run it

Skills You'll Need to Bring: 

5+ years in technical program management, business systems, finance transformation, or a related field, with substantial time on finance or revenue systems; public-company or IPO-track experience is a strong plus

Working fluency in finance operations; you don't need to be an accountant, but you should hold your own on quote-to-cash and record-to-report, and know why revenue recognition is not the same as billing

Hands-on ITGC program experience across access, change management, and IT operations for in-scope financial systems, plus practical SOX knowledge. You understand how ITGC reliance determines what auditors will accept from automated controls and system-generated reports, can tell a key control from a non-key one, know where ITACs fit alongside ITGCs, and have been through remediation and audit cycles rather than only reading about them

AI-native operating mindset; this is a core requirement for this role. You already use AI to draft requirements, synthesize status, triage intake, and assemble evidence packages, and you share the patterns so others work differently because of what you built

A track record of independently delivering technical programs end to end, ideally transformation work such as system modernization, a large-scale migration, or an ERP or billing platform implementation, and turning messy or incomplete inputs into a concrete plan with owners and dates; you're pulled into problems before they're scoped and you're as useful advising a controller on process design as an engineering lead on sequencing

Working understanding of data lifecycle and analytics tooling, and real experience running change management for business systems, not just launching them

Influence without authority and a bias toward closure. You have no direct reports, so you work through credibility and clear reasoning, knowing when to push and when to escalate; you chase ambiguous items to a decision, will reopen the uncomfortable question a week before launch, and communicate clearly with Director/VP+ stakeholders, including when the news is bad

Nice to Haves:

Hands-on experience working in enterprise billing, ERP, and revenue systems such as NetSuite, Stripe, or comparable tools, with an understanding of how orders, invoices, and revenue data flow between them

Experience supporting an IPO readiness or first-year SOX program, including standing up ITGCs from scratch

CISA, CIA, or equivalent certification, or equivalent time embedded on an IT audit team

Experience building internal tooling or agents on a workspace platform rather than only configuring vendor systems

If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase.

Team/ Role Paragraph: The Knowledge Systems team builds the infrastructure powering accurate knowledge across customer self-service, internal tools, and AI-assisted support. As Technical Program Manager, you will translate knowledge strategy into technical execution. This is a systems-focused role bridging customer experience, knowledge operations, and technical delivery to build the foundation required to scale support without scaling headcount linearly.

 

What you’ll do: 

  • Own technical programs that improve the systems, tooling, and workflows behind customer self-service, internal support knowledge, and AI-assisted discovery (e.g., RAG pipelines, semantic search, and agentic workflows).
  • Drive cross-functional alignment across Knowledge Systems, engineering, product, and partner teams to translate complex knowledge taxonomies and unstructured data into clear technical specifications, APIs, schemas, and execution plans.
  • Lead the planning and delivery of high-leverage initiatives such as workflow automation, knowledge system modernization, CMS improvements, metadata and structure enhancements, and launch-readiness tooling.
  • Partner with Knowledge Systems leads to ensure knowledge is accurate, structured for machine-readability and actionability, ready ahead of launch, and governed appropriately for customer, specialist, and compliance needs.
  • Build and run an operating cadence for technical initiatives, including roadmap tracking, dependency management, risk escalation, and delivery accountability.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce manual work, improve scale, and prevent headcount from growing linearly with business complexity and launch volume.

Required skills and experience:

  • 5+ years of technical program management, systems implementation, or operational program leadership in a complex cross-functional environment.
  • Deep familiarity with modern information retrieval architectures (such as vector databases, RAG, and LLM orchestration tools like LangChain or LlamaIndex) alongside CMS platforms, structured content, and metadata models.
  • Strong systems thinking and operational judgment, with the ability to connect technical decisions to customer impact, specialist usability, compliance risk, and business performance.
  • Experience translating operational strategy into technical requirements, data schemas, and tooling investments.
  • Strong understanding of content systems, knowledge management, workflow automation, and internal tooling in operations or CX environments.
  • Proven ability to drive alignment across technical and non-technical stakeholders, especially where ownership is distributed and tradeoffs must be actively managed.
  • Demonstrated experience leading ambiguous, multi-team initiatives from concept through launch with clear accountability, risk management, and measurable outcomes.
  • Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality

As a Sr Technical Program Manager, you are instrumental in advancing our Forward Deployed Engineering team's mission, which is dedicated to accelerating and de-risking our customers' outcomes by ensuring the success of every project we undertake. Your role is pivotal in not only achieving project goals but also in maintaining an exceptional level of customer satisfaction throughout the process. You will expertly navigate the balance between delivering outstanding results and aligning with the commercial objectives of the Forward Deployed Engineering organization. Your leadership and strategic insight will contribute directly to our clients' success and the growth of our business.

 

The impact you will have:

  • You will take ownership of all commercial delivery of services from a project administration and director perspective across numerous projects, ranging from a single individual for 2-3 weeks to 6-month engagements of multi-person teams
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to senior customer stakeholders, driving clarity, alignment, and confidence through all stages of delivery

The Program Management Office (PMO) at Zoox is at the center of the company's efforts, responsible for driving cross-functional program planning and execution at the highest level. We partner with leaders from every corner of the company—vehicle development, software engineering, manufacturing, and operations—to deliver on the ambitious milestones that pave our path to launching a revolutionary autonomous mobility service.
The L3 Program within PMO is responsible for the optimal allocation and usage of the test fleet, operated nationwide, with leading-edge hardware and software that will be used in future milestones. Our program managers contribute to the end to end success of all of Zoox's technical, integrated product milestones on our purpose-built robotaxi.
We are excited to launch a new initiative to bring exceptional early-career talent into our PMO team. This is a role for those who have a history of high performance in their academic and project work and are eager to apply their skills to complex, real-world challenges. While we hire for potential and rate of learning, we are looking for individuals who have demonstrated the ability to perform at a high level, regardless of their years of experience. 
As a Technical Program Manager (6-month contract), you will be given concrete, well-defined projects that will allow you to make a real impact from the start. About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

Examples of key problems the team is working on
